definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.
For nonzero integers a,b,c,d with a+b+c+d=0, let N1>=N2>=N3>=N4 be the decreasing rearrangement of |a|,|b|,|c|,|d|, and Third(a,b,c,d)=N3. Ties may be ordered arbitrarily.

output.statement: For all nonnegative sequences x1,x2,x3,x4 in ell^2(Z\{0}), sum_(a+b+c+d=0,abcd!=0) x1(a)x2(b)x3(c)x4(d)/Third(a,b,c,d)<=C product_(r=1)^4||xr||_(ell^2). The same bound holds after restricting the sum to any subset.

locals.declaration: Fix arbitrary nonnegative ell^2 sequence x1; first prove the bound for finite support, then truncate.
Fix arbitrary nonnegative ell^2 sequence x2; first prove the bound for finite support, then truncate.
Fix arbitrary nonnegative ell^2 sequence x3; first prove the bound for finite support, then truncate.
Fix arbitrary nonnegative ell^2 sequence x4; first prove the bound for finite support, then truncate.
Set X_(r,j)=||xr 1_(2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1))||_ell2, j>=0, with negative shell indices assigned zero.

argument.text: Begin with finite support. Decompose each sequence into shells 2^j<=|k|<2^(j+1), j>=0, with shell norms X_(r,j). Fix one of the at most 24 orderings of the four shell indices, and relabel slots within this calculation so j1>=j2>=j3>=j4. A nonzero zero-sum interaction has j1-j2<=2: otherwise the largest magnitude is at least 2^(j2+3), exceeding three times the upper magnitude 2^(j2+1) of the remaining entries. For fixed values of the two smaller frequencies, the sum of the two large-frequency sequences constrained by the zero sum is <=X_(1,j1)X_(2,j2) by Cauchy–Schwarz (translated reflection preserves the ell2 norm). A shell has 2^(j+1) integer entries, so summing the two small sequences in ell1 gives <=C*2^((j3+j4)/2)*product_r X_(r,jr). Dividing by Third>=2^j3 leaves C*2^(-(j3-j4)/2).

produces.statement: For each ordered shell interaction j1>=j2>=j3>=j4 with j1-j2 in {0,1,2}, its weighted contribution is <=C 2^(-(j3-j4)/2) product_r X_(r,jr).

argument.text: For each q=j1-j2 in {0,1,2}, enlarge the nonnegative sum by dropping the upper restriction on the smaller indices. Its bound factors as C*(sum_J X_(1,J)X_(2,J-q))*(sum_(ell>=m)2^(-(ell-m)/2)X_(3,ell)X_(4,m)). The first factor is <=||X_1||_ell2||X_2||_ell2. Write r=ell-m in the second and apply Cauchy–Schwarz for each fixed r; it is <=sum_(r>=0)2^(-r/2)||X_3||_ell2||X_4||_ell2=(1-2^(-1/2))^(-1)||X_3||_ell2||X_4||_ell2. The shell norm squares sum to the original norm square. Summing over the orderings and three offsets proves the finite-support estimate.

produces.statement: The asserted four-linear estimate holds for all nonnegative finite-support sequences with one absolute support-independent constant.

argument.text: For arbitrary nonnegative ell2 sequences restrict each to |k|<=m. Their norms are no larger than the full norms. Every finite set of interaction terms occurs in some such truncation; hence the infinite positive sum is the supremum of these finite sums and has the same bound. Restricting to a subset only decreases a nonnegative sum. This proves both assertions without an exchange of conditionally convergent sums.
